topic_candidates.title: Apple’s Folding iPhone Might Have a Hinge Problem!
topic_candidates.query: iFixit iPhone Duo teardown hinge support bar screen cracks October 2026
topic_candidates.brief: The video starts with the reports of inner screens cracking after very little use, then follows the teardown to show how a folding screen survives thousands of bends. Instead of declaring a recall, it separates confirmed observations from possible causes: dust entering the hinge, a support bar not retracting fully, or a hinge rail pressing against the OLED. The viewer learns why a tiny alignment error can create a much larger failure on an expensive foldable phone.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: iFixit’s teardown confirms the Duo’s hinge, display and dust-protection design and reconstructs possible stress points using teardown footage, CT scans and Apple patents. Independent reporting documents multiple early screen-failure reports, but the precise failure rate and final cause remain unconfirmed. The story should therefore frame the mechanism as an engineering hypothesis, not a proven universal defect.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Foldable OLEDs must tolerate repeated bending while remaining extremely thin. Stress concentrates at edges, hinge transitions and support surfaces; microscopic particles or a fraction of a millimeter of interference can turn repeated flexing into a crack or dead-pixel line.

topic_candidates.title: The End of Data Centres? Apple and Meta’s Bet Beyond the Cloud | AI Decoded
topic_candidates.query: Apple Meta on-device AI local models data centers cloud computing 2026
topic_candidates.brief: The video asks whether every AI request really needs to travel to a giant data center. It explains the emerging split: small, private and fast tasks can run on a phone or desktop, while larger jobs still need server farms. Apple’s on-device and Private Cloud Compute approach is compared with Meta’s push toward AI hardware and open-weight models, giving viewers a practical answer about battery life, privacy, speed and why data centers are not disappearing overnight.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Apple says its AI architecture combines on-device models with Private Cloud Compute for requests that need more computing power, and that some workloads can run on third-party data centers while preserving its stated privacy design. Meta separately describes its MTIA chips as part of a continuing data-center strategy, so the evidence supports a hybrid future rather than the end of cloud infrastructure.
topic_candidates.science_angle: The trade-off is between compute density and data locality. Local inference reduces network delay and can keep personal data on a device, but larger models need more memory, energy and parallel processing than consumer hardware can usually provide.

topic_candidates.title: China just dropped a new frontier model... and nobody can explain why
topic_candidates.query: Moonshot AI Kimi K3.1 Pro open-weight model 2.8 trillion parameters one million context October 2026
topic_candidates.brief: The video explains what is genuinely surprising about Kimi K3.1 Pro without treating benchmark claims as magic. It shows how a model can advertise nearly three trillion total parameters while activating only a fraction for each token, why that makes it more practical than a dense model of the same size, and what “open-weight” actually means for researchers and companies. The final question is whether cheaper access and future weights release could make frontier-level tools less dependent on a few American labs.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Moonshot’s Kimi K3 technical material describes a mixture-of-experts architecture with roughly 2.8 trillion total parameters, about 104 billion active per token and a one-million-token context window. Major technology reporting says Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained upgrade in the same model family and that its strongest performance claims are based primarily on company-reported benchmarks, so independent results should be distinguished from marketing claims.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Mixture-of-experts models contain many specialist subnetworks but route each token through only a subset. This lowers the compute required per token compared with activating every parameter, although memory, training cost and serving complexity can still be enormous.
